prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1327; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane at a traffic signal in Pasadena, Texas, when the vehicle behind them, operated by Driver 2, failed to stop and struck the rear bumper of Driver 1's vehicle. Passenger was seated in the front passenger position at the time of impact. Passenger reported pain in the right knee and was able to step out of the vehicle with some assistance and was transported for evaluation. The knee complaint is consistent with the force of a rear impact of this kind, where an occupant's leg can strike the dashboard or lower console. Driver 2 acknowledged the collision at the scene and did not dispute how it occurred. Two independent witnesses in a nearby vehicle gave statements that matched the sequence described by both drivers, and scene photographs show damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle and the front of Driver 2's vehicle that lines up with the reported point and direction of impact. No prior damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle was noted during the inspection. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Officers observed Passenger in the vehicle immediately after the collision and confirmed their presence with both drivers.
